question: Does the incumbent attention-mass (TF) ranker already capture slot IMPORTANCE, or is there headroom for an information-theoretic selector? Concretely: how do six per-slot scores (tf_mass, entropy, leave-one-out KL, diagonal Fisher of the QA loss, linear redundancy of the value vector, MT/QA contrast) rank-correlate on the Phase-1 cartridge, how differently would each select the top-32 slots, and how much larger is the 'safe acquisition budget' under an importance metric than under attention mass (~9% from DIAG-ROUTING's 0.914 top-32 overlap)?
variable_under_test: none - forward passes plus diagnostic backward passes on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge; QA vs MT eval splits. No knob was changed and nothing was trained.
baseline_ref: DIAG-ROUTING (same cartridge, same eval-time softmax convention) / DIAG-OVERWRITE (the incumbent ranker's actual per-document selections)

numbers.note: No training and no eval-harness run: no CE loss is reported as a result (WORKERS.md: never fabricate a number). The Fisher pass does recompute the harness's own per-token CE, and its token-weighted micro-average is reported under diagnostics.per_example_micro_mean_ce_from_fisher_pass as a plumbing check. mass_on_S is not applicable: no AM write was performed; the closest quantity, the per-slot eval-time attention mass, IS the primary measurement here.

fp32_precision_control.note: one packed QA batch recomputed with model+cache in float32 and autocast off; the primary Fisher uses the eval harness's own bf16 autocast path.

attenuation_corrected_spearman.note: observed Spearman divided by sqrt(rel_x*rel_y); reliabilities are split-half Spearman corrected to full sample size by Spearman-Brown. An UPPER bound on the true correlation. redundancy is deterministic (reliability 1).

selector_tradeoff_table._definition: per layer: fraction of the 511 writable slots' mean MT routing mass captured by the 32 selected slots (write bandwidth), fraction of total QA diagonal-Fisher mass sitting in those same 32 slots (retention risk), and their mean redundancy. Higher bandwidth / lower Fisher is better.

command: TAG=full NBOOT=500 FP32_CHECK=1 bash research_loop/results/DIAG-IMPORTANCE/launch_diag_importance.sh  (backgrounded; claims one GPU by flock, exports PYTHONPATH=/tmp/amsnap_DIAG-IMPORTANCE from `git archive HEAD`, then runs research_loop/results/DIAG-IMPORTANCE/measure_slot_importance.py on outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/cache_last.pt over both eval parquets). NO file under cartridges/ or examples/ was edited; three new standalone files were created under research_loop/results/DIAG-IMPORTANCE/.

provenance.routing_vector_definition: a(q) = softmax(qK_cart^T/sqrt(d)) over the 512 cartridge slots, recovered as w[:, :T_c]/w[:, :T_c].sum() from the FULL eval-time softmax over [512 slots || own-sequence causal prefix]; == value_solve.py:86 X at top_t=512. Identical to DIAG-ROUTING.
provenance.per_layer_aggregation: scores are summed over the 8 KV heads AND the 4 query heads in each GQA group, matching the incumbent ranker's per_layer granularity
provenance.ranker_score_definition: softmax(mean_over_GQA_group(q) @ trainable_keys^T / sqrt(d)) summed over kv-heads and query positions -- the exact convention of query_accum.py:80-95 (group mean taken BEFORE the softmax; frozen slot 0 excluded)

observations: GATE. The pipeline reproduces DIAG-ROUTING on the shared quantities to 4-5 significant figures (per-head QA/MT top-32 overlap 0.91417 vs 0.914; mean-routing cosine 0.998989 vs 0.99899; histogram intersection 0.96299 vs 0.963), and the differentiable forward used for the Fisher pass recovers the Phase-1 cartridge's own CE to 2.23779 QA / 3.78930 MT against the published 2.23881 / 3.78255 (-0.0010 / +0.0068, inside the board's known 0.0065 in-run-vs-standalone harness spread and far inside DIAG-NOISE's paired band). HEADLINE: attention mass does NOT capture importance. Spearman(tf_mass_qa, fisher) = 0.579 pooled (bootstrap 95% CI [0.559, 0.613]) and 0.666 +/- 0.122 per layer (range 0.471 at L5 to 0.924 at L35); disattenuating by the split-half reliabilities (tf_mass 0.990, fisher 0.952 after Spearman-Brown) raises these only to 0.596 / 0.686, so 0.9 is excluded by a wide margin and the pooled value sits at the brief's 0.6 threshold. kl_loo is NOT an independent signal: per-layer Spearman with tf_mass_qa is 0.968 (0.978 disattenuated), which is what the algebra predicts - the exact leave-one-out KL is -log(1-w_j), a convex reweighting of the same mass. Entropy is nearly orthogonal per layer (0.237 with mass, -0.198 with Fisher). The strongest non-gradient correlate of Fisher is redundancy, Spearman -0.648 pooled [-0.650, -0.629] (-0.323 per layer): slots whose value vector is well reconstructed from the other 511 carry little QA Fisher. Redundancy needs no eval data at all (one 512x512 inverse per layer) and is stable across three ridge levels (Spearman 0.999999). SELECTION. The incumbent ranker is essentially a pure attention-mass selector, and every importance-based selector would pick a nearly disjoint set: per-layer top-32 overlap with the incumbent is 83.3% for tf_mass_qa and 84.0% for tf_mass_mt but 10.7% for the 32 most-redundant slots, 1.0% for highest-contrast, 0.4% for lowest-entropy, 0.09% for lowest-Fisher and 0.00% for lowest-kl_loo. The eval-query reproduction of the ranker matches the canonical run's own saved per-document masks by 54.1% (60.9% on doc 0, 47.1% on doc 15). SAFE ACQUISITION BUDGET (MT-wanted = per-layer top-32 by tf_mass_mt). Under attention, 6.9% of MT's wanted slots fall outside QA's top-32 (bootstrap 8.7% [5.4, 15.0], matching the ~9% the board inferred from the 0.914 overlap) and 0.0% fall in QA's bottom half. Under Fisher, 62.9% [60.0, 67.0] fall outside QA's Fisher-top-32 - a 9.2x larger set - but only 11.2% [7.6, 13.9] fall in the safest half and 2.3% in the safest quartile. Under redundancy: 83.7% / 42.1% / 22.9%, and 9.6% land in the safest 32 slots. CONCENTRATION. QA importance is concentrated: per layer the top-32 of 511 slots hold 52.4% of the QA Fisher mass (36.5-81.0% across layers), top-64 66.8%, top-128 82.1%, participation ratio 64.3 of 511. Attention mass is markedly more diffuse (top-32 39.5%, PR 113.1). THE TRADE-OFF, measured directly. The incumbent's 32 slots/layer capture 37.4% of the writable MT routing mass and sit on 29.6% of all QA Fisher mass. Selecting the best 32 slots inside the safest QA Fisher quartile instead gives 4.62% MT mass and 0.28% QA Fisher - a 106x reduction in QA exposure for an 8.1x reduction in write bandwidth. The most-redundant quartile gives a middle point: 17.3% MT mass / 12.3% QA Fisher (2.4x less exposure for 2.2x less bandwidth). Joint availability confirms the geometry: of MT's top-32 per layer only 0.72 slots are also in the safest Fisher quartile against a chance value of 8.0 (11x BELOW chance), whereas 7.33 are in the most-redundant quartile (at chance). COST AND CONTROLS. The Fisher diagnostic is 147 backward passes = 98.8 s (QA 73.5 s, MT 25.3 s); gradient_steps is 0 (no optimizer exists, .grad is read then zeroed, the cache is never written). The attention pass is 3.2 s for QA. The optional float32 control (one packed QA batch with model and cache in fp32, autocast off, 343 s dominated by flex_attention recompilation) gives Spearman(bf16, fp32) = 0.99966, so bf16 is not a limitation. Total wall clock 692 s on one flock-claimed GPU. CAVEATS. Only one correlation is unresolved: tf_mass_qa vs contrast, bootstrap CI [-0.248, +0.085], spanning zero. The incumbent reproduction uses MT *eval* queries against Phase-1 keys, not the MT synthesis conversations against the evolving cartridge, and agrees with the actual masks only 54.1% of the time. Fisher is the empirical (not true) Fisher on 78 QA / 69 MT examples with split-half reliability 0.908 / 0.934. kl_loo is a single-layer local measure with no propagation of the deletion through the network. All numbers are on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge, before any AM write.
interpretation_requested_by_the_brief_no: An information-theoretic selector DOES have headroom over the incumbent TF ranker - the family is not bounded by the correlation test. Attention mass explains only Spearman 0.58-0.69 of diagonal-Fisher importance (disattenuated), so the two orderings genuinely differ, and the selections differ almost completely: top-32 overlap with the incumbent is 0.1% for a Fisher-safest selector and 10.7% for a redundancy-safest selector, against the incumbent's 83-84% agreement with plain attention mass. The safe budget grows from Y = 6.9% (attention) to 62.9% (Fisher) and 83.7% (redundancy) on the 'outside QA's own top-32' definition; on the stricter 'in QA's safest half' definition it grows from 0.0% to 11.2% (Fisher) and 42.1% (redundancy). QA importance is also concentrated enough to leave room (52.4% of QA Fisher mass in 32 of 511 slots per layer). But the headroom is on the axis the project has already won. The measured Pareto trade is 106x less QA Fisher exposure for 8.1x less MT write bandwidth (37.4% -> 4.62% of writable MT routing mass), because MT-wanted and QA-Fisher-safe are ANTI-aligned - their intersection is 11x below chance. A protective gater would therefore buy retention, which is already 0.34-0.49 ahead of the 2.52 budget, by spending acquisition bandwidth, which is the entire remaining deficit. Redundancy is the exception worth naming: it is the only metric whose intersection with MT-wanted is at chance rather than below it, it correlates with Fisher at -0.648 pooled, and it costs one 512x512 inverse per layer with no eval data and no gradients. This is a measured result about slot scores only; it says nothing about what any selector would do to CE, which no run in this bundle measured.
